subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and if so which public config shape should own it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change adds public config surface and changes how tool-deny security boundaries flow from requester agents to subagents.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides listed tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Use the per-spawn toolsAllow direction for child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate agent profiles or instructions until a later design.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy only
options.body: Reject parent-deny delegation for now and document the security rationale plus separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides listed tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior and controlled child inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest available routing signal for a new security-boundary config/API decision across subagent and tool-policy history.
